response:
## 1) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Webhook-triggered `updateMany` with empty data may not update anything and adds a write to every webhook

Affected:
- packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1022-1024

Explanation:
`updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` relies on Prisma's `@updatedAt` being applied even when `data` is empty. That behaviour is not guaranteed. An empty `updateMany` can end up as a no-op, so `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` would never change.

Even if it does work, the value is never read by the UI. The dropdown shows `CalendarCache.updatedAt` through `cacheUpdatedAt`. So this adds an unconditional DB write on every Google webhook or cache refresh for no visible benefit.

It is also unclear from the diff whether `SelectedCalendarRepository` is imported in this file. For delegation credentials, `this.credential.id` may not match the `credentialId` stored on the rows.

Fix: either remove the call, or set the timestamp explicitly so it does not depend on implicit `@updatedAt` behaviour.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, { updatedAt: new Date() });
// or remove the call entirely, since the UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt
~~~

## 2) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: Use the update-many input type in `updateManyByCredentialId`

Affected:
- packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.ts:400-405

Explanation:
`prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany` expects `SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput` or `UncheckedUpdateManyInput`. `SelectedCalendarUpdateInput` includes relation operations such as `user: { connect }`, which `updateMany` does not accept. This is likely a TypeScript error. If it is cast through, relation payloads would fail at runtime.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
static async updateManyByCredentialId(
  credentialId: number,
  data: Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput
) {
  return await prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data });
}
~~~

## 3) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug
Title: `deleteCache` throws a generic Error and rejects credentials the UI lets users act on

Affected:
- packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:17-30
- packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:67-69

Explanation:
A plain `Error` reaches tRPC as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) instead of NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN, and the message is surfaced as a server fault.

There is also a mismatch with the UI. The dropdown shows "Delete cached data" for any Google credential that has a cache, including delegation-credential calendars (`hasCache` ignores `delegationCredentialId`). The handler, however, only accepts credentials where `userId === user.id`. Delegation and team credentials will therefore always fail with an error toast.

The handler also bypasses `CalendarCacheRepository`, even though `deleteManyByCredential` already exists. That breaks the repository pattern the PR adopted elsewhere.

Fix: throw a `TRPCError`, use the repository, and hide the delete action for credentials the user cannot manage.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
import { TRPCError } from "@trpc/server";
...
if (!credential) throw new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND", message: "Credential not found" });
await new CalendarCacheRepository().deleteManyByCredential(credentialId);
~~~
~~~tsx
const hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && !!cacheUpdatedAt && !delegationCredentialId;
~~~

## 4) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Cache status includes expired entries and shows misleading timestamps for legacy rows

Affected:
- packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:173-188
- packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:1-9

Explanation:
`groupBy` does not filter on `expiresAt`. A credential whose cache has fully expired will still show a "Last updated" status and the delete option.

The migration backfills every existing row with `NOW()`. Old cache entries will therefore display the migration time as their last update.

The migration header comment also says the column is added "without a default value", which contradicts the SQL below it.

Fix: add a `where: { expiresAt: { gte: new Date() } }` filter, and correct the comment.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds }, expiresAt: { gte: new Date() } },
~~~

## 5) Severity: LOW | Type: Implementation
Title: Format the timestamp with the user's locale instead of hardcoded "en-US"

Affected:
- packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:88-94

Explanation:
The timestamp is always formatted in US style, whatever the user's language or locale setting is. Use the `i18n.language` value from `useLocale()` instead.

Proposed fix:
~~~tsx
const { t, i18n } = useLocale();
new Intl.DateTimeFormat(i18n.language, { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" }).format(new Date(cacheUpdatedAt))
~~~

## 6) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: Remove unused `updatedAt`/`googleChannelId` fields from the user select

Affected:
- packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts:899-900
- packages/lib/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts:21-28

Explanation:
These fields were added for the earlier per-calendar dropdown design. After the refactor to a credential-level dropdown, nothing in the diff uses them.

Leaving them in widens the types and the queries. It may also send Google channel IDs to the client unnecessarily. Remove them if they are no longer used.

Proposed fix:
~~~ts
// remove updatedAt: true, googleChannelId: true and revert the Pick types
~~~

## 7) Severity: LOW | Type: Bug
Title: Make the dev script portable and independent of the working directory

Affected:
- scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:5
- scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:12-18
- scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:68

Explanation:
`sed -i ''` only works with BSD/macOS sed. On GNU sed (Linux) it fails or misbehaves.

`ENV_FILE="../.env"` depends on the caller's working directory, so the script may create or edit the wrong `.env` file.

`cleanup` always exits with status 0, even on failure paths such as the rate limit or a missing URL. That hides errors from callers.

Fix: resolve paths relative to the script, use portable in-place editing, and exit non-zero on errors.

Proposed fix:
~~~bash
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
ENV_FILE="$SCRIPT_DIR/../.env"
...
sed -E "s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=.*|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=$TUNNEL_URL|" "$ENV_FILE" > "$ENV_FILE.tmp" && mv "$ENV_FILE.tmp" "$ENV_FILE"
~~~

## 8) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability
Title: `dev:cron` relies on `npx tsx` without a declared dependency

Affected:
- apps/web/package.json:11

Explanation:
If `tsx` is not a declared devDependency, `npx` will download an unpinned version at runtime. That makes the script non-reproducible and needs network access.

Fix: add `tsx` as a devDependency and call `tsx` directly.

Proposed fix:
~~~json
"dev:cron": "tsx cron-tester.ts"
~~~
